ui.privacy.intro: This page explains how Raasta handles your information under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Raasta is a free project. It has no accounts and no login.
ui.privacy.accounts: You do not need to sign up or log in. We do not ask for your name, phone number or email address to use Raasta. The feedback forms ask for a contact only if you choose to give one.
ui.privacy.server: Raasta does not keep your personal details on our servers. When you describe a problem, the text is handled in memory to produce your guidance, and it is not written to a log. Letters and forms are built in memory and sent back to you.
ui.privacy.ai: Some features send text to an AI provider to be put into plain language. Before that happens, we remove phone numbers, email addresses, Aadhaar and PAN numbers, bank and card numbers, UPI IDs and one-time codes. Where a provider's service allows it, we ask that it does not keep or train on this text.
ui.privacy.cookies: Raasta sets two cookies only. raasta_lang remembers the language you chose. raasta_loc remembers the state or city you entered, if you entered one. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.
ui.privacy.drafts: If you choose to save a draft, it is kept in your browser's local storage on your device. We cannot see it. The button below removes everything Raasta has saved on this device.
ui.privacy.cleared: Everything Raasta saved on this device has been cleared.
ui.privacy.clear_fail: Raasta could not clear local storage in this browser. You can clear the site data in your browser settings.
ui.privacy.feedback: Feedback and requests for new complaint systems are stored in a database. They are not linked to your name. Please do not include personal details in them.
ui.privacy.refs: When a complaint is sent through a government platform such as DIGIT, Raasta keeps only the reference ID that the platform gives back, so that you can follow it up.
ui.privacy.rights: You can ask what Raasta holds about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. You can also complain about how we handle your information. Send your complaint through the feedback page. The Grievance Officer for Raasta is the project team, reached through the feedback page.

ui.terms.intro: These terms apply when you use Raasta. By using Raasta, you agree to them.
ui.terms.law: These terms are governed by the laws of India. Any dispute about Raasta is subject to the jurisdiction of the courts in Pune, Maharashtra.
ui.terms.advice: Raasta gives procedural guidance based on public government rules. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create a lawyer and client relationship. For advice about your case, speak to a lawyer or to free legal aid.
ui.terms.warranty: Raasta is provided as it is. We try to keep information correct and up to date, but rules, fees and office details change. Check with the authority before you act. We are not liable for loss that comes from using or relying on Raasta.
ui.terms.use: Use Raasta only for lawful purposes, for your own problem, or to help someone who has asked you to. Do not try to break into the site, overload it, or send false complaints. Do not paste other people's personal details.
ui.terms.content: Government portals, offices and phone numbers belong to the bodies that run them. Raasta lists them for your convenience and does not control them. Map data comes from OpenStreetMap contributors under the Open Database Licence.
ui.terms.changes: We may change these terms. The date at the bottom of this page shows when they last changed.
ui.terms.contact: Questions about these terms can be sent through the feedback page.
ui.disclaimer.lead: Raasta gives procedural guidance based on public government rules. It is not legal advice.
ui.disclaimer.p1: Raasta explains which authority usually handles a kind of problem, what the first peaceful step is, which documents are often needed, and which time limits apply under the rules we have recorded.
ui.disclaimer.p2: Every case is different. Rules change, offices change their procedures, and the facts of your case decide the best route. Check details with the authority, and get advice from a qualified lawyer or free legal aid when the matter is serious.
ui.disclaimer.p3: Fees, time limits and office details come from our sources, and we show the date we last checked them. If a link or phone number does not work, please tell us through the feedback page.
ui.disclaimer.p4: Never share an OTP, PIN, password or card number with anyone who asks for it by message or call, including someone who says they are from Raasta.
ui.about.lead: Raasta helps people in India find the right authority for an everyday dispute.
ui.about.who: Raasta was built by a student team for the Rotary x Rotaract Naya Bharat 2047 Code for Bharat hackathon. The team is not a company, and Raasta is free to use.
ui.about.how_lead: Each request passes through five stages.
ui.about.how.1: Understanding. Raasta reads what you describe in your own words and picks out the kind of problem. Personal details are removed first.
ui.about.how.2: Finding the place. Raasta works out your state, district and city, and your ward where we have the boundaries, so that it can match local offices.
ui.about.how.3: Choosing the route. A fixed set of rules, written from public handbooks, decides the first peaceful step, the right authority and the next steps. These rules do not use AI.
ui.about.how.4: Explaining it. An AI helper may put the result into plain language. It can only repeat facts that the rules already contain, and it cannot add links, fees or deadlines of its own.
ui.about.how.5: Acting on it. You get a checklist, a letter or form to check, a step-by-step guide and contact details. You read what Raasta prepares and send it yourself.
ui.about.not: Raasta is not a government service, a law firm or a court. It does not file a case for you.
